value.body: An Integrated PhD (also called Int-PhD or M.Sc–PhD) admits students straight after a B.Sc into a programme that combines master's-level coursework with doctoral research. It is offered by research institutes such as IISc, the IISERs, TIFR and some universities, mainly in the sciences.

items.label: Duration
items.note: Varies by institute and research progress

items.label: Students enrolled
items.note: Programmes reported under this name; some institutes record such students as PhD

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc (some programmes also take other bachelor's degrees) with a minimum percentage. Selection uses national tests — JEST (physics, theoretical computer science), IIT JAM or GATE, depending on the subject — or an institute's own test such as the TIFR Graduate School admission test, followed by interviews. Each institute lists which scores it accepts.

value.title: At a glance
items: Students usually receive a scholarship during coursework and a research fellowship later, per institute norms.
Many programmes allow an exit with a master's degree after the coursework phase.
It is a long commitment aimed at a research career.
Outcomes include postdoctoral research, academic posts and research roles in labs and industry.

value.title: Integrated PhD enrolment
value.note: Row 'Integrated Ph.D-Integrated Doctor of Philosophy'. Some institutes may report these students under M.Sc or Ph.D rows instead. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth or decline.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 programme-wise enrolment, based on actual responses (Ministry of Education)
